summary: Most quantified commitments in Croatia's submission are framed at EU level rather than as Croatia-specific allocations. For conservation, the EU LULUCF target is 310 million tonnes of CO2 equivalent in net removals by 2030. Restoration measures are to cover at least 20% of EU land areas and 20% of EU sea areas by 2030, with measures in place for all ecosystems that need restoration by 2050. The reported potential from rewetting and restoring peatlands and wetlands is 51–54 Mt CO2-eq/yr. The mixed, biodiversity-respecting reforestation and sustainable-forest-management measure has a reported potential of 8–235 Mt CO2-eq/yr, while improved fertiliser-use efficiency is associated with 19 Mt CO2-eq/yr in agriculture. Croatia's current cover includes 26,444 km² of forest (46.7%), 23,631 km² of agriculture (41.8%) and 315 km² of wetland (0.6%), but no quantified Croatian shares are given.
